newsitem.title: USA: Outback shares tumble on weak sales.
newsitem.headline: Outback shares tumble on weak sales.

text.p: Outback Steakhouse Inc. stock fell Friday after the restaurant chain said its comparable-store sales dropped more sharply than expected in December.
Outback lost $1.50 to $26 on Nasdaq on volume of more than 680,000 shares, more than double Outback's average daily volume of about 340,000 shares.

An Outback spokeswoman confirmed that the Tampa, Fla.-based chain told analysts Thursday that sales at units open at least a year fell 3.2 percent in December and dropped 2.4 percent for the fourth quarter.
The spokeswoman attributed the decline in part to the shorter period between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
The slowdown was larger than expected, according to traders and anaylsts.
Alex. Brown analysts Steven Rockwell and David Trossman said they were expecting a 1 percent drop in fourth-quarter same-store sales and called the December figure "disappointing."
The analysts trimmed Outback's earnings estimates but preserved their "strong buy" recommendation.
The analysts cut their estimate of 1997 earnings to $1.75 a share from $1.79 a share, and their 1998 forecast to $2.20 a share from $2.25. Their 1996 estimate was $1.45 a share.
Outback earned $53.6 million, or $1.15 a share, in 1995 on sales of $664 million. The company, with 330 restaurants in 33 states, went public in June 1991.
